build_common_tools_justification: Dockerfile, pip and npm, driven by GitHub Actions.
build_floss_tools_justification: Docker or podman, Python, Node and npm are all FLOSS, and nothing in the build needs a proprietary tool.
build_justification: The software is shipped as a container built from the Dockerfile, and the release workflow rebuilds it from source for every tagged release.
contribution_justification: Contributions are issue-first pull requests to main, squash-merged after review; the process is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the requirements: an issue per change, the branch-name prefixes, Closes N in the pull request, tests and docs with each change, and the local gates to run before opening one. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is not implemented here: the project calls hashlib, hmac and secrets from the Python standard library, and botocore s SigV4 signer.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography comes from Python s standard library and botocore, both FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: SHA-256 hashes, 32-byte random tokens and 16-byte salts meet the NIST 2030 minimums for hash and symmetric material.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Passwords are stored as PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 260000 iterations and a 16-byte per-user salt, in a self-describing salted format.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project terminates no TLS itself: HTTPS is provided by GitHub Pages and GHCR, and the gateway forwards signed requests over the operator s own network.
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for passwords, SHA-256 digests for sessions and tokens, and AWS Signature Version 4 for outgoing calls.
crypto_random_justification: secrets.token_urlsafe and secrets.token_bytes generate every session, reset token, API token, account identifier and salt.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: SHA-256 throughout, with no SHA-1 dependency.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4, MD5, DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG, and no custom cipher mode, appears in the project.
delivery_mitm_justification: The image is pulled from ghcr.io over HTTPS, releases are served by GitHub over HTTPS, and the site is served by GitHub Pages over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is distributed over plain HTTP; releases publish SHA256SUMS and the image digest over HTTPS.
description: A control plane, console and gateway in front of an AWS emulator
description_good_justification: The documentation opens by naming the problem: an AWS emulator gives you the AWS APIs on one host and one credential but no accounts, sign-in or console, so a team cannot share it. Emuplane adds those parts and is plainly not an emulator itself. https://mathewmusango.github.io/emuplane/docs/intro/
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions are public, searchable and URL-addressable, and open to new participants. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/discussions
documentation_basics_justification: The documentation covers installing and starting the image, the first account and first bucket, every console page, configuration, and the security model and limits. https://mathewmusango.github.io/emuplane/docs/intro/
documentation_interface_justification: The control API reference is generated from the console route table and lists every route and method. https://mathewmusango.github.io/emuplane/docs/reference/control-api/
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The pytest and vitest suites assert throughout, and the live-lab policy and bucket-policy matrices assert every cell of the expected decision.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is in use, so no finding from one has been raised.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzer or input-varying analyser runs against a release, and branch coverage is not measured, so the 80 percent test-suite alternative cannot be claimed yet.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project is written in Python and JavaScript, neither of which is a memory-unsafe language.
english_justification: All documentation and all issue and pull request discussion are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request to date was answered and then either implemented or explicitly declined in, for example, the S3 console work and the declined accelerate/request-payment/bucket-location areas.
floss_license_justification: Released under the MIT licence, full text in LICENSE at the repository root.
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
interact_justification: The site documents obtaining the image from ghcr.io, reporting bugs and enhancement requests through GitHub Issues and Discussions, and the contribution process. https://mathewmusango.github.io/emuplane/contributing/
know_common_errors_justification: Input validation, path traversal, script injection, missing authorisation and session replay are each named in the scope list of SECURITY.md and handled in the code.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the trust boundary in SECURITY.md: sessions stored as digests, least privilege between accounts, fail-closed gateway rules and a stated deployment model.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: releases v0.1.0 through v0.8.0, a documented release process, weekly dependency and security scans, and issues answered and closed as they arrive.
name: Emuplane
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed: .env files are gitignored, the deployment bearer token is minted inside the container, and the example deployments carry no real secret.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md is written per release from the closed issues, and each GitHub release carries human-readable notes with an SBOM, checksums and the image digest. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability with a CVE assignment, or similar, has been fixed in any release to date; the project is pre-1.0 and has no such history.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main as a reviewed pull request between releases, and each release is prepared as a pull request of its own.
repo_public_justification: The repository is public at https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane
repo_track_justification: Git history records what changed, who changed it and when; main is pull-request-only and squash-merged.
report_archive_justification: Public issue archive, searchable and permanent. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/issues
report_process_justification: Bugs and enhancement requests are filed as GitHub issues, with a bug-report template. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed to date has been triaged, answered and closed by the maintainer, generally the same day; there are no unanswered reports.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the issue tracker, with labels and a project board.
sites_https_justification: The documentation site, the repository and the container registry are all served over HTTPS.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL s security queries and Semgrep s rules look for injection, path traversal, unsafe request handling and similar classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Every medium or higher alert is either fixed in code or dismissed on the alert with a written reason; both scanners report 0 open alerts on the default branch.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL and Semgrep run on every push and pull request, with ruff as an additional lint gate.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL and Semgrep run on every push and pull request, while Scorecard, Trivy and the dependency audit also run on a schedule.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: tests.yml, checks.yml, codeql.yml, semgrep.yml, security.yml and trivy.yml run on every push to main and every pull request.
test_invocation_justification: Standard invocations: python -m pytest at the repository root and npm test in web/.
test_justification: pytest covers the control plane, the gateway rules and the S3 surface, and vitest covers the console pages; both run in CI and on every pull request. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml
test_most_justification: The suites cover the control API routes, the gateway authorisation rules, the S3 console surface and the console pages including the error paths.
test_policy_justification: Every feature lands with tests in the same pull request, and a ledger test pins the coverage classification so a new operation cannot be added without one.
tests_are_added_justification: Every module since v0.1.0 shipped with its own tests, the v0.2.0 S3 work added control and console tests alongside every new page, and the trend holds through v0.8.0: this cycle added the release-plan, triage and badge gates with tests of their own.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests with each change and names the commands that run them.
version_tags_justification: Annotated git tags from v0.1.0 to v0.8.0.
version_unique_justification: Every release is tagged vX.Y.Z and the container image carries the same version tag.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported, and dependency and code-scanning alerts are answered as they appear.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known medium or higher vulnerability is unpatched; Dependabot, CodeQL, Semgrep and Trivy are clean at the v0.8.0 release.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Security then Report a vulnerability opens a private advisory visible only to the reporter and the maintainer; encrypted email is offered as an alternative. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the private reporting route: GitHub private vulnerability reporting, with email as an alternative, and asks for no public issue. https://github.com/mathewmusango/emuplane/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last six months.
warnings_fixed_justification: ruff is clean repo-wide and CI fails on any finding; tsc is clean.
warnings_justification: ruff with a configured ruleset for Python, and tsc --noEmit together with the vitest suite for the console.
warnings_strict_justification: Both are configured as strictly as the project uses them in CI: tsc with strict enabled, ruff with its configured correctness rules, and each fails the build rather than warn.
